Headline PCE, which includes food and energy, rose 0.3% on the month and 2.8% from a year earlier, above consensus estimates for increases of 0.44% and 2.9%.

data.headline: The Fed’s Preferred Inflation Gauge Is Likely to Flash Red Ahead of the March Policy Meeting
data.summary: The Federal Reserve’s preferred inflation gauge, the personal consumption expenditures price index, is expected to show price pressures remained firm in January.  Economists expect the PCE index data–which the Bureau of Economic Analysis is due to release at 8:30 a.m. Eastern on Friday–to show headline inflation rose 0.33% in January from the prior month and 2.9% from a year earlier, according to consensus estimates compiled by FactSet.  Core PCE, which strips out volatile food and energy prices and carries more weight with the Fed, is expected to rise 0.41% on the month and 2.9% from a year ago.
